title: Telemetry ingest migration coordinator: compatibility bridge for SDK/CLI/API
creator: Aarya Patel
description: Problem: multiple telemetry producers (SDKs, CLI, Console backend) are emitting variants of our analytics events. Changes to the event schema have caused downstream pipeline regressions and left us with brittle parsing logic in the ingestion layer. Goal: build a Migration Coordinator service plus lightweight compatibility adapters that allow new SDK/CLI/API schema versions to be accepted safely while migrating pipelines and dashboards. The coordinator will orchestrate staged rollouts, transform/validate events, emit compatibility metrics, and provide a schema registry interface for the Console backend and ingestion pipeline teams.
motivation: Reduce incident blast radius from schema changes, enable independent SDK/CLI/API evolution, and provide observability for A/B/schema variant traffic during rollouts so that console analytics dashboards and billing/usage metrics remain accurate.
acceptance_criteria: Migration Coordinator service deployed to staging and receives a mirrored subset of production telemetry.
SDK/CLI adapters implemented for v2 and v3 event envelopes and pass contract tests.
Schema registry endpoint available; ingestion pipeline can query active compatibility rules.
Transformation rules implement safe defaulting and preserve token-level cost fields required by billing pipelines.
End-to-end canary: 5% of Console traffic routed through coordinator for 72h with no data loss and less than 1% discrepancy in cost metrics.
Automated contract tests run in CI for PRs touching SDKs, CLI, and ingestion connectors.
Runbook and rollback playbook written and reviewed by SRE and Product.
Security review completed for transformation logic and stored schemas (KMS access pattern documented).
design_decisions: Implement coordinator as a lightweight, horizontally scalable service in the console backend cluster to minimize cross-cluster latency.
Adapters will live in SDK and CLI repos; coordinator exposes a validation/transform API to minimize breaking changes.
Prefer declarative transformations via JSONPath + mapping rules stored in schema registry rather than hardcoded glue logic to allow fast updates without deploys.
Use event sample hashing and consistent routing to ensure canary traffic hits the same downstream pipeline partitions for reproducible comparisons.
tasks: Spec schema registry API and storage (S3 + Dynamo index) — design doc linked.
Build migration coordinator prototype: validation, transform, metrics emission (Prometheus + tracing).
Create SDK/CLI adapter prototypes for v2->canonical and v3->canonical transformations.
Integrate contract test harness into SDK/CLI CI and ingestion pipeline CI.
Create dashboards comparing pre/post metrics (latency, events/sec, cost tokens, missing fields).
Run 5% canary in staging for 72h, then 25% in production with SRE oversight.
Complete security review and update RBAC/KMS docs for schema access.
updates: 2026-02-12: Ticket created by Aarya — initial scoping and risk assessment. Linked to PM-812.
2026-02-18: Decision to colocate coordinator in console backend after perf analysis (Jonas). Slight trade-off: tighter coupling vs lower latency.
2026-02-25: Prototype registry API sketched in design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Telemetry+Migration+Coordinator

2026-03-03: Security flagged encryption-at-rest requirement for stored schemas; added to acceptance criteria.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Transformation logic may drop subtle billing fields — Mitigation: strict contract tests + validation gate before enabling a rule.
Risk: Increased latency for request paths that call coordinator — Mitigation: caching of transformation rules and local LRU prefix test, colocate service.
Risk: Multiple SDK versions create combinatorial explosion — Mitigation: focus on maintaining canonical envelope and adapters only for active major versions; deprecate older versions with telemetry.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on transformation rule expressiveness and CI gating for contract tests. Expect follow-up design doc for scaling rules to 100k events/sec. Ensure SRE runbook is realistic for 3am rollbacks.
